assumptions: The supplied CRA reporting dates and deadlines apply to the target manufacturers.
Customers will pay separately for preparation rather than relying solely on public guidance.
A qualified MSSP and counsel can be contracted without exhausting target margins.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid tabletop engagements converting to retainers, documented response-time improvements, insurable liability terms, and a signed 24/7 MSSP partnership with enforceable incident SLAs.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A rehearsed evidence-assembly process addresses the mismatch between short statutory incident clocks and fragmented manufacturer telemetry, legal judgment, and corrective actions.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines create severe downside, but willingness to buy retainers before incidents and segment-specific budgets are unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid readiness retainers plus surge fees can be valuable, but reserved expert capacity, counsel, insurance, and bursty utilization constrain margins and scale.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: CEE connected-product manufacturers form a meaningful segment, although applicability, readiness gaps, and reachable buyers are not quantified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: MSSPs, insurers, law firms, and product-security vendors have superior trust, credentials, telemetry access, and bundling positions.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The dossier relationship can expand into product-security documentation, vulnerability handling, tabletop exercises, conformity readiness, and ongoing governance.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Product-specific evidence maps and rehearsals create switching costs, but mandates are nonexclusive, customer-controlled, and readily transferred to established advisers.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Pre-assembled dossiers can materially reduce response time, yet no SLA performance or superiority over incumbent incident-response retainers is established.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Reporting obligations begin now and broader CRA requirements follow, creating a strong readiness window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Conformity assessors, insurers, development houses, and MSSPs are logical channels, but they can appropriate the offer and no partner commitment is present.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A solo part-time founder cannot credibly deliver 24/7 high-liability response; success requires contracted cyber, legal, and operational coverage with binding SLAs.

highest_value_structural_change: Make an established MSSP the accountable 24/7 delivery partner while the business owns standardized CRA dossier preparation and recurring customer readiness workflows.
main_structural_strength: An urgent statutory clock makes preparedness economically legible and supports recurring readiness revenue before incidents occur.
primary_score_limiter: The delivery promise requires continuous expert coverage, security trust, and liability capacity that the founder does not possess independently.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The official platform and guidance simplify submission, while real incidents are bursty and require 24/7 staffing beyond a solo founder.
